decisions.reason: The hard-return spacing decision concerns paragraph entry behavior; it does not change the candidate's legacy copy-paste workflow, test sources, or target version.
Changing hard-return spacing does not alter the independent requirement that pasted tables and columns remain within page bounds.
The source distinguishes excessive spacing in continuous text from spacing that already fits bullet points; it does not change the required bullet appearance.
The candidate already requires Enter-based multiline input, while the source modification independently governs spacing produced by hard returns in continuous text.
Appropriate hard-return spacing does not change the separate requirement for fixed margins and prevention of pencil-icon clipping.
Paragraph and line-break behavior has no necessary effect on which theme colors are available.
The unintended border created after a Topic row is a separate structural behavior and is not changed by the hard-return spacing decision.
The source modification concerns line-break spacing, not automatic removal of placeholder text when fields are activated.
The required style-set contents and cross-template coverage remain unchanged by the paragraph-spacing decision.
The source decision changes a product behavior and does not alter the earlier task-local assessment method, budget, or outputs.
Hard-return spacing does not change the selected editable-field mechanism or the handling of password-dependent legacy controls.
The source explicitly treats bullet-point spacing as acceptable and does not change Tab-based hierarchy or nested-list alignment.
